dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] De-duplicate `existing` before the remove loop (or make the unlink+relink transactional) so a pre-existing duplicate caused_by edge does not make the second `remove_dependency` raise and abort before the new edge is written.
evidence: transition_close.py:245-247: `for superseded in existing:` then `remove_dependency(ticket_id, superseded, tracker_dir, "caused_by")` then `_write_link_event(...)`
_active_caused_by_targets returns a plain list with no de-dup: transition_close.py:177-181
ticket 10d0 description: two distinct link_uuids with the SAME target_id both appear in deps — the reducer surfaces both, so `existing` becomes `[origin, origin]` for such tickets
unlink.py:128-134: `_write_unlink` raises CommandError when no active link exists between source and target
The unlink+link sequence is not atomic and any raise lands in the broad `except Exception` at transition_close.py:248, aborting before the new edge is written
dropped.finding: The REPLACE branch iterates `for superseded in existing` and calls `remove_dependency` once per list element, but `existing` (from `_active_caused_by_targets`) can contain the SAME target twice on a ticket carrying a pre-existing duplicate caused_by edge (the exact corruption bug 10d0 produced). The second `remove_dependency` for that target finds no net-active link and raises CommandError, which the outer `except` swallows AFTER the first unlink but BEFORE `_write_link_event` runs — so the corrected culprit is never written and the edge set is left partially mutated.
scenarios: Closing a bug that already carries two net-active caused_by edges to the same target (pre-existing corruption) with a DIFFERENT explicit --caused-by
dropped.suggested_fix: Iterate over `dict.fromkeys(existing)` (or a set) in the remove loop so each target is unlinked once; the relation-scoped `remove_dependency` already removes the net-active link, and add_dependency-side history handles the rest.
